title: Block and File Storage
description: Compare EBS volume types, EBS snapshots, EFS, and FSx for Windows and Lustre.

data.text: AWS provides three main types of storage: object storage (S3), block storage (EBS), and file storage (EFS and FSx). Each type is designed for specific use cases. Block storage provides low-latency raw storage volumes. File storage provides shared file systems that multiple instances can access simultaneously.

Elastic Block Store (EBS) provides persistent block storage volumes for EC2. EBS volumes are tied to a single Availability Zone and persist independently from the instance life. Snapshots let you back up volumes to S3 and restore them to new volumes.

Elastic File System (EFS) provides a simple, scalable, elastic file system for Linux-based workloads. Multiple EC2 instances can mount the same EFS file system simultaneously, making it ideal for content management, web serving, and shared data processing.

Amazon FSx is a fully managed file system service with two offerings: FSx for Windows File Server provides a native Windows file system with SMB support, Active Directory integration, and distributed file caching. FSx for Lustre is a high-performance file system optimized for machine learning, analytics, and high-performance computing.

data.title: Choosing the Right Storage
items: Use EBS when you need a single instance to access block storage with low latency.
Use EFS when multiple Linux instances need shared access to the same files.
Use FSx for Windows when you need a Windows-native file system with Active Directory.
Use FSx for Lustre when you need high throughput for HPC or ML workloads.
Use S3 for object storage, backups, and static content.

terms.definition: A block storage device that can be attached to a single EC2 instance.
An incremental backup of an EBS volume stored in Amazon S3.
Elastic File System — a managed NFS file system for shared Linux access.
A fully managed Windows file server with SMB support and AD integration.
A high-performance file system optimized for HPC and machine learning.

data.title: Mount an EFS File System
data.content: This example shows how to mount an EFS file system on an EC2 instance running Amazon Linux.
data.code:
# Install the EFS mount helper on Amazon Linux
sudo yum install -y amazon-efs-utils

# Create a mount directory
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/efs

# Mount the EFS file system
sudo mount -t efs fs-12345678:/ /mnt/efs

# Verify the mount
ls /mnt/efs

# Add to fstab for automatic mounting on reboot
echo "fs-12345678:/ /mnt/efs efs _netdev,tls,iam 0 0" | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: EBS provides block storage for single-instance workloads
EBS snapshots provide incremental backups stored in S3
EFS provides shared file storage for Linux instances
FSx for Windows provides native Windows file sharing
FSx for Lustre provides high-performance storage for HPC and ML
